quotes.text: "After that I lived like a young rajah in all the capitals of Europe—Paris, Venice, Rome—collecting jewels, chiefly rubies, hunting big game, painting a little, things for myself only, and trying to forget something very sad that had happened to me long ago."

quotes.text: "Then came the war, old sport. It was a great relief and I tried very hard to die but I seemed to bear an enchanted life. I accepted a commission as first lieutenant when it began. We stayed there two days and two nights, a hundred and thirty men with sixteen Lewis guns, and when the infantry came up at last they found the insignia of three German divisions among the piles of dead. I was promoted to be a major and every Allied government gave me a decoration—even Montenegro, little Montenegro down on the Adriatic Sea!"

quotes.text: "You're causing a row. Please have a little self control."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I suppose the latest thing is to sit back and let Mr. Nobody from Nowhere make love to your wife. Well, if that's the idea you can count me out… . Nowadays people begin by sneering at family life and family institutions and next they'll throw everything overboard and have intermarriage between black and white."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I know I'm not very popular. I don't give big parties. I suppose you've got to make your house into a pigsty in order to have any friends—in the modern world."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I've got something to tell you, old sport,——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Please let's all go home. Why don't we all go home?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come on, Tom. Nobody wants a drink."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I want to know what Mr. Gatsby has to tell me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She's never loved you. She loves me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She never loved you, do you hear?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She only married you because I was poor and she was tired of waiting for me. It was a terrible mistake, but in her heart she never loved any one except me!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's been going on? I want to hear all about it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I told you what's been going on,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Going on for five years—and you didn't know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You've been seeing this fellow for five years?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, we couldn't meet. But both of us loved each other all that time, old sport, and you didn't know. I used to laugh sometimes—"but there was no laughter in his eyes, "to think that you didn't know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I can't speak about what happened five years ago, because I didn't know Daisy then—and I'll be damned if I see how you got within a mile of her unless you brought the groceries to the back door. But all the rest of that's a God Damned lie. Daisy loved me when she married me and she loves me now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She does, though. The trouble is that sometimes she gets foolish ideas in her head and doesn't know what she's doing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And what's more, I love Daisy too. Once in a while I go off on a spree and make a fool of myself, but I always come back, and in my heart I love her all the time."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Do you know why we left Chicago? I'm surprised that they didn't treat you to the story of that little spree."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It doesn't matter any more. Just tell him the truth—that you never loved him—and it's all wiped out forever."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not that day I carried you down from the Punch Bowl to keep your shoes dry?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I love you now—isn't that enough? I can't help what's past."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I did love him once—but I loved you too."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She didn't know you were alive. Why,—there're things between Daisy and me that you'll never know, things that neither of us can ever forget."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I want to speak to Daisy alone,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Even alone I can't say I never loved Tom,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course it matters. I'm going to take better care of you from now on."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You're not going to take care of her any more."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Certainly not for a common swindler who'd have to steal the ring he put on her finger."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You're one of that bunch that hangs around with Meyer Wolfshiem—that much I happen to know. I've made a little investigation into your affairs—and I'll carry it further tomorrow."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You can suit yourself about that, old sport."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I found out what your 'drug stores' were."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He and this Wolfshiem bought up a lot of side-street drug stores here and in Chicago and sold grain alcohol over the counter. That's one of his little stunts. I picked him for a bootlegger the first time I saw him and I wasn't far wrong."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I guess your friend Walter Chase wasn't too proud to come in on it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And you left him in the lurch, didn't you? You let him go to jail for a month over in New Jersey. God! You ought to hear Walter on the subject of you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He came to us dead broke. He was very glad to pick up some money, old sport."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Walter could have you up on the betting laws too, but Wolfshiem scared him into shutting his mouth."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That drug store business was just small change,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "but you've got something on now that Walter's afraid to tell me about."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Please, Tom! I can't stand this any more."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Go on. He won't annoy you. I think he realizes that his presumptuous little flirtation is over."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Want any of this stuff? Jordan? … Nick?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No … I just remembered that today's my birthday."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I've got my wife locked in up there,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She's going to stay there till the day after tomorrow and then we're going to move away."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Throw me down and beat me, you dirty little coward!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's good. Wilson'll have a little business at last."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "O, my Ga-od! O, my Ga-od! Oh, Ga-od! Oh, my Ga-od!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What happened—that's what I want to know!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She ran out ina road. Son-of-a-bitch didn't even stopus car."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "—she ran out there an' the one comin' from N'York knock right into her goin' thirty or forty miles an hour."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's the name of this place here?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, but the car passed me down the road, going faster'n forty. Going fifty, sixty."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come here and let's have your name. Look out now. I want to get his name."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You don't have to tell me what kind of car it was! I know what kind of car it was!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I just got here a minute ago, from New York. I was bringing you that coupé we've been talking about. That yellow car I was driving this afternoon wasn't mine, do you hear? I haven't seen it all afternoon."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He says he knows the car that did it… . It was a yellow car."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Now, if you'll let me have that name again correct——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "If somebody'll come here and sit with him!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I ought to have dropped you in West Egg, Nick. There's nothing we can do tonight."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'll telephone for a taxi to take you home, and while you're waiting you and Jordan better go in the kitchen and have them get you some supper—if you want any."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No thanks. But I'd be glad if you'd order me the taxi. I'll wait outside."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Did you see any trouble on the road?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I thought so; I told Daisy I thought so. It's better that the shock should all come at once. She stood it pretty well."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I got to West Egg by a side road,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and left the car in my garage. I don't think anybody saw us but of course I can't be sure."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Her name was Wilson. Her husband owns the garage. How the devil did it happen?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, I tried to swing the wheel——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "but of course I'll say I was. You see, when we left New York she was very nervous and she thought it would steady her to drive—and this woman rushed out at us just as we were passing a car coming the other way. It all happened in a minute but it seemed to me that she wanted to speak to us, thought we were somebody she knew. Well, first Daisy turned away from the woman toward the other car, and then she lost her nerve and turned back. The second my hand reached the wheel I felt the shock—it must have killed her instantly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Anyhow—Daisy stepped on it. I tried to make her stop, but she couldn't so I pulled on the emergency brake. Then she fell over into my lap and I drove on.



"She'll be all right tomorrow,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm just going to wait here and see if he tries to bother her about that unpleasantness this afternoon. She's locked herself into her room and if he tries any brutality she's going to turn the light out and on again."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How long are you going to wait?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All night if necessary. Anyhow till they all go to bed."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'll see if there's any sign of a commotion."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You'd better come home and get some sleep."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I want to wait here till Daisy goes to bed. Good night, old sport."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I waited, and about four o'clock she came to the window and stood there for a minute and then turned out the light."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's pretty certain they'll trace your car."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Go to Atlantic City for a week, or up to Montreal."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I can't describe to you how surprised I was to find out I loved her, old sport. I even hoped for a while that she'd throw me over, but she didn't, because she was in love with me too. She thought I knew a lot because I knew different things from her… . Well, there I was, way off my ambitions, getting deeper in love every minute, and all of a sudden I didn't care. What was the use of doing great things if I could have a better time telling her what I was going to do?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't think she ever loved him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You must remember, old sport, she was very excited this afternoon. He told her those things in a way that frightened her—that made it look as if I was some kind of cheap sharper. And the result was she hardly knew what she was saying."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course she might have loved him, just for a minute, when they were first married—and loved me more even then, do you see?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm going to drain the pool today, Mr. Gatsby. Leaves'll start falling pretty soon and then there's always trouble with the pipes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You know, old sport, I've never used that pool all summer?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You're worth the whole damn bunch put together."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm at Hempstead and I'm going down to Southampton this afternoon."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You weren't so nice to me last night."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Suppose I don't go to Southampton, and come into town this afternoon?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How long have you been married, George? Come on there, try and sit still a minute and answer my question. How long have you been married?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Ever had any children? Come on, George, sit still—I asked you a question. Did you ever have any children?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Have you got a church you go to sometimes, George? Maybe even if you haven't been there for a long time? Maybe I could call up the church and get a priest to come over and he could talk to you, see?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You ought to have a church, George, for times like this. You must have gone to church once. Didn't you get married in a church? Listen, George, listen to me. Didn't you get married in a church?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I found it yesterday afternoon. She tried to tell me about it but I knew it was something funny."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She had it wrapped in tissue paper on her bureau."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I have a way of finding out."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "This has been a strain to you and you don't know what you're saying. You'd better try and sit quiet till morning."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm one of these trusting fellas and I don't think any harm to nobody, but when I get to know a thing I know it. It was the man in that car. She ran out to speak to him and he wouldn't stop."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How could she of been like that?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Maybe you got some friend that I could telephone for, George?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I told her she might fool me but she couldn't fool God. I took her to the window—"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "—and I said 'God knows what you've been doing, everything you've been doing. You may fool me but you can't fool God!' "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Any idea where they are? How I could reach them?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'll get somebody for you, Gatsby. Don't worry. Just trust me and I'll get somebody for you——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Look here, old sport, you've got to get somebody for me. You've got to try hard. I can't go through this alone."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Hell of a note, isn't it? Get my wire?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "They picked him up when he handed the bonds over the counter. They got a circular from New York giving 'em the numbers just five minutes before. What d'you know about that, hey? You never can tell in these hick towns——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Look here—this isn't Mr. Gatsby. Mr. Gatsby's dead."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I saw it in the Chicago newspaper,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It was all in the Chicago newspaper. I started right away."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I didn't know how to reach you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't want anything. I'm all right now, Mr.——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, I'm all right now. Where have they got Jimmy?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I didn't know what you'd want, Mr. Gatsby——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "—Mr. Gatz. I thought you might want to take the body west."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Jimmy always liked it better down East. He rose up to his position in the East. Were you a friend of my boy's, Mr.—?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He had a big future before him, you know. He was only a young man but he had a lot of brain power here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "If he'd of lived he'd of been a great man. A man like James J. Hill. He'd of helped build up the country."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Three o'clock, here at the house. I wish you'd tell anybody who'd be interested."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course I'm not likely to see anybody, but if I do."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, I'll certainly try. What I called up about is——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, the fact is—the truth of the matter is that I'm staying with some people up here in Greenwich and they rather expect me to be with them tomorrow. In fact there's a sort of picnic or something. Of course I'll do my very best to get away."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What I called up about was a pair of shoes I left there. I wonder if it'd be too much trouble to have the butler send them on. You see they're tennis shoes and I'm sort of helpless without them. My address is care of B. F.——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Please say that Mr. Carraway wants to see him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I can't get him back from Chicago, can I?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'll give it to him when he gets back."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You young men think you can force your way in here any time,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "We're getting sickantired of it. When I say he's in Chicago, he's in Chicago."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My memory goes back to when I first met him,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "A young major just out of the army and covered over with medals he got in the war. He was so hard up he had to keep on wearing his uniform because he couldn't buy some regular clothes. First time I saw him was when he come into Winebrenner's poolroom at Forty-third Street and asked for a job. He hadn't eat anything for a couple of days. 'Come on have some lunch with me,' I sid. He ate more than four dollars' worth of food in half an hour."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I raised him up out of nothing, right out of the gutter. I saw right away he was a fine appearing, gentlemanly young man, and when he told me he was an Oggsford I knew I could use him good. I got him to join up in the American Legion and he used to stand high there. Right off he did some work for a client of mine up to Albany. We were so thick like that in everything—"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You were his closest friend, so I know you'll want to come to his funeral this afternoon."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I can't do it—I can't get mixed up in it,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There's nothing to get mixed up in. It's all over now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "When a man gets killed I never like to get mixed up in it in any way. I keep out. When I was a young man it was different—if a friend of mine died, no matter how, I stuck with them to the end. You may think that's sentimental but I mean it—to the bitter end."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let us learn to show our friendship for a man when he is alive and not after he is dead,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "After that my own rule is to let everything alone."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Jimmy sent it to me. I think it's a very pretty picture. It shows up well."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Very well. Had you seen him lately?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He come out to see me two years ago and bought me the house I live in now. Of course we was broke up when he run off from home but I see now there was a reason for it. He knew he had a big future in front of him. And ever since he made a success he was very generous with me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Look here, this is a book he had when he was a boy. It just shows you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"



Practice elocution, poise and how to attain it 5.00-6.00 "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"







GENERAL RESOLVES







No wasting time at Shafters or [a name, indecipherable]



No more smokeing or chewing



Bath every other day



Read one improving book or magazine per week



Save $5.00 [crossed out] $3.00 per week



Be better to parents







"I come across this book by accident,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Jimmy was bound to get ahead. He always had some resolves like this or something. Do you notice what he's got about improving his mind? He was always great for that. He told me I et like a hog once and I beat him for it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Blessed are the dead that the rain falls on,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, my God! they used to go there by the hundreds."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Are you going to the Ordways'? the Herseys'? the Schultzes'?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You threw me over on the telephone. I don't give a damn about you now but it was a new experience for me and I felt a little dizzy for a while."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "——a conversation we had once about driving a car?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You said a bad driver was only safe until she met another bad driver? Well, I met another bad driver, didn't I? I mean it was careless of me to make such a wrong guess. I thought you were rather an honest, straightforward person. I thought it was your secret pride."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm five years too old to lie to myself and call it honor."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's the matter, Nick? Do you object to shaking hands with me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes. You know what I think of you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Crazy as hell. I don't know what's the matter with you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "what did you say to Wilson that afternoon?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He came to the door while we were getting ready to leave and when I sent down word that we weren't in he tried to force his way upstairs. He was crazy enough to kill me if I hadn't told him who owned the car. His hand was on a revolver in his pocket every minute he was in the house——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What if I did tell him? That fellow had it coming to him. He threw dust into your eyes just like he did in Daisy's but he was a tough one. He ran over Myrtle like you'd run over a dog and never even stopped his car."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And if you think I didn't have my share of suffering—look here, when I went to give up that flat and saw that damn box of dog biscuits sitting there on the sideboard I sat down and cried like a baby. By God it was awful——"
quotes.speaker: Unknown
